stories.title: Helium-3 lifts new quantum computing concept with faster tunneling rates
stories.desc: Helium—the lightest atom that can be laser-cooled and controlled—powers a new design for high-powered, stable quantum computers.

stories.desc: How did a photon survive a journey of more than 2 billion light-years when, according to known physics, it should have been absorbed long before reaching Earth? stories.title: Superfluid qubit could help scale up quantum computers
stories.desc: Superfluid helium could offer a new way to tackle one of the biggest challenges in scaling up quantum computers, say researchers from the University of Surrey. The research team has introduced a conceptual design for a new type of qubit that could be much less vulnerable to errors.

stories.title: Wastewater Can Take Harmful Algal Blooms from Bad to Worse
stories.desc: By modeling toxic diatoms and coastal processes, scientists have discovered the degree to which nutrients from Southern California’s densely populated coast affect these blooms.

stories.title: Anak Krakatau Rumbles Again
stories.desc: A powerful eruption from the Indonesian volcano lofted ash into the atmosphere, disrupting thousands of flights and degrading air quality. The post Anak Krakatau Rumbles Again appeared first on NASA Science .
